subject: NBA
text: The NBA player game-log table was tested in a browser on 20 November 2026. Its URL pattern is nba.com/stats/player/<id>/boxscores-traditional.

subject: NFL
text: The NFL player game-log table was tested in a browser on 20 November 2026. Its URL pattern is nfl.com/players/<slug>/stats/logs/. Older seasons use the season choice on that page.

subject: Method
text: A trend uses one player or team, one stat, a threshold you type, and the last 5, 10 or 20 games played, or the season. It may be split by home, away or opponent.

subject: Method
text: The five rate bands are under 40%, 40 to 59%, 60 to 69%, 70 to 79%, and 80% and over.

subject: Method
text: Walk through games in date order across this season and the previous one. After each game, use the window ending at that game. A rate in the current band makes a spot. Games after the spot cannot choose it.

subject: Method
text: After a spot, count threshold reaches in the next 5 games the subject played. The next spot for that band cannot start until those games have passed. Within that calculation, each later game counts once.

subject: Method
text: Pool the later games as x of y, with a Wilson 95% range. The end of a season may leave fewer than 5 games after a spot. Under 15 later games, show “too few past spots to tell” and no score.

subject: Method
text: Count games the subject played. Skip missed games in both the window and the later games. Player minutes and snaps are outside the first version.

subject: Method
text: When a provider corrects a stat, the next nightly file will carry it. Rates and scores will be worked out again from the stored logs. No result will be kept across nights.

subject: Method
text: The number for a kind of trend pools subjects within a league, for the same stat family, window and band. It has its own counts.
